questions.prompt: In Oracle 12c, what is the difference between a System Privilege and an Object Privilege?

options.text: System privileges govern database-wide actions (e.g., CREATE SESSION); Object privileges govern actions on specific schema objects (e.g., SELECT ON hr.employees)
Object privileges apply only to tablespaces
System privileges cannot be revoked
They are synonyms

questions.explanation: Oracle separates instance/schema-level capabilities (system privileges) from object-scoped operations (object privileges).

questions.prompt: In an Oracle 12c Multitenant CDB, which naming convention and clause are required by default when creating a Common User in CDB$ROOT?

options.text: Prefix with C## (per COMMON_USER_PREFIX) and specify CONTAINER=ALL
Prefix with PDB_ and specify CONTAINER=CURRENT
No prefix is needed in CDB$ROOT
Common users can only be created inside a PDB

questions.explanation: Oracle 12c requires common users created in CDB$ROOT to start with `C##` (unless COMMON_USER_PREFIX is changed) and applies across containers with `CONTAINER=ALL`.

rubric.label: Applies Oracle 12c CDB/PDB common user rules

questions.prompt: Which Oracle 12c administrative privilege was introduced to separate backup/recovery duties from full SYSDBA data access (least privilege)?

options.text: SYSBACKUP
DBA_ALL
CONNECT
RESOURCE

questions.explanation: Oracle 12c introduced SYSBACKUP, SYSDG, and SYSKM to enforce separation of duties without granting full SYSDBA.

questions.prompt: User A grants `SELECT ON sales TO User B WITH GRANT OPTION`, and User B grants it to User C. What happens when User A revokes `SELECT ON sales FROM User B`?

options.text: User C retains SELECT indefinitely
The revoke cascades and User C also loses SELECT ON sales
Oracle throws ORA-01927 and refuses to revoke
The sales table is dropped

questions.explanation: Object privileges granted WITH GRANT OPTION cascade on REVOKE (unlike system privileges granted WITH ADMIN OPTION, which do not cascade).

questions.prompt: Select ALL security hardening practices recommended for an Oracle 12c production database.

options.text: Enforce password complexity & failed-login lockouts via Oracle Profiles
Enable Unified Auditing for privileged/DDL actions
Grant DBA role to every application service account
Restrict PUBLIC execute privileges on powerful packages like UTL_HTTP

questions.explanation: Least privilege, Profiles, Unified Auditing, and locking down PUBLIC packages reduce blast radius dramatically.

questions.prompt: An application team requests `DBA` privileges for their reporting user in an Oracle 12c PDB. Explain how you deny this safely and design a least-privilege role instead.
questions.explanation: Deny DBA, create a dedicated PDB-local read-only role with CREATE SESSION and explicit SELECT grants on required views/tables, and enforce resource limits via a Profile.

rubric.label: Enforces least privilege with scoped role
Uses PDB-local role and Profile limits

questions.prompt: Why must an Oracle 12c database run in `ARCHIVELOG` mode to perform hot (online) RMAN backups and point-in-time recovery (PITR)?

options.text: NOARCHIVELOG mode disables SQL SELECT queries
ARCHIVELOG preserves filled online redo logs as archived redo logs so RMAN can recover transactions after the backup snapshot
RMAN cannot read control files otherwise
ARCHIVELOG compresses datafiles by 90%

questions.explanation: Without archived redo logs, online redo logs are overwritten, making online consistent recovery and PITR impossible.

rubric.label: Links ARCHIVELOG to online backup & PITR

questions.prompt: In Oracle 12c RMAN, what is the difference between a Differential (default) and a Cumulative Level 1 incremental backup?

options.text: Differential backs up blocks changed since the last Level 0 OR Level 1 backup; Cumulative backs up all blocks changed since the last Level 0 backup
Cumulative backs up only the control file
Differential cannot be restored without Data Pump
They produce identical backup sizes

questions.explanation: Cumulative Level 1 backups are larger than Differential but reduce recovery time by needing fewer incremental pieces.

rubric.label: Understands backup size vs recovery speed trade-off

questions.prompt: Which RMAN command verifies that backups exist on disk/tape and marks missing files as EXPIRED in the RMAN repository?

options.text: CROSSCHECK BACKUP
DELETE FORCE ALL
ALTER SYSTEM SWITCH LOGFILE
SHUTDOWN ABORT

questions.explanation: CROSSCHECK BACKUP reconciles RMAN metadata against physical storage; DELETE EXPIRED BACKUP then cleans stale records.

questions.prompt: A single data block in a 2 TB tablespace is reported corrupt (`ORA-01578`) while the database is open. Which Oracle 12c RMAN feature repairs it with minimal downtime?

options.text: Full database drop and impdp
RMAN Block Media Recovery (`RECOVER DATAFILE ... BLOCK ...` or `RECOVER CORRUPTION LIST`)
TRUNCATE TABLE
Disabling the controlfile autobackup

questions.explanation: Block Media Recovery restores and recovers only the corrupted block(s) while the rest of the datafile remains online.

questions.prompt: Select ALL essential practices for a resilient Oracle 12c RMAN backup strategy.

options.text: Enable `CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE AUTOBACKUP ON`
Regularly test restore/recovery onto an isolated non-prod host
Store RMAN backups exclusively on the same disk array as live datafiles
Configure a retention policy (e.g., RECOVERY WINDOW OF 7 DAYS) aligned to RPO/RTO

questions.explanation: Controlfile autobackup, off-host storage, retention policies, and tested restores ensure backups are actually recoverable.

questions.prompt: A user accidentally ran `DROP TABLE billing_ledger PURGE` at 14:12 in an Oracle 12c PDB running in ARCHIVELOG mode. Outline your RMAN recovery plan (12c Table Recovery or PDB PITR) to minimize impact.
questions.explanation: Use Oracle 12c RMAN `RECOVER TABLE` (using an auxiliary instance to recover to 14:11 and Data Pump import the table) without taking the whole CDB/PDB offline, or PDB PITR if dependencies require.

rubric.label: Minimizes blast radius to other PDBs

questions.prompt: On the orders_ops dataset, write a query returning each order status, order count (order_count), and total revenue (total_revenue), ordered by total_revenue descending.
questions.hint: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
questions.starterCode:
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY 
ORDER BY ;
questions.explanation: Aggregates order volume and revenue by status cleanly in a single scan.

rubric.label: Aggregates COUNT and SUM per status

questions.prompt: Using the employees dataset, list departments whose total payroll (total_payroll) exceeds 15000, returning department and total_payroll ordered by total_payroll descending.
questions.starterCode:
SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_payroll
FROM employees
GROUP BY 
HAVING 
ORDER BY total_payroll DESC;
questions.explanation: Computes departmental payroll totals and filters via HAVING > 15000.

questions.prompt: On orders_ops, find the single highest-value PAID order per customer tier. Return tier and max_order_amount ordered by tier ascending.
questions.hint: JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'PAID' GROUP BY c.tier.
questions.starterCode:
SELECT c.tier, MAX(o.total_amount) AS max_order_amount
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE 
GROUP BY 
ORDER BY c.tier ASC;
questions.explanation: Joins customers to PAID orders and computes MAX(total_amount) per tier.

questions.prompt: In Oracle 12c, a query filters `WHERE TRUNC(order_date) = DATE '2026-02-01'` on a standard B-tree index on `order_date`. Why does the optimizer perform a Full Table Scan?

options.text: B-tree indexes do not support DATE columns
Wrapping the indexed column in `TRUNC()` prevents standard index range scans unless a function-based index exists or the predicate is rewritten as a range
Oracle ignores WHERE clauses on dates
Full table scans are always required for single dates

questions.explanation: Rewriting as `order_date >= DATE '2026-02-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-02-02'` makes the predicate sargable for the existing B-tree index.

questions.prompt: Which Oracle 12c diagnostic report compares instance wait events, top SQL by elapsed time/buffer gets, and load profile between two snapshots?

options.text: AWR (Automatic Workload Repository) Report
Listener.ora log
SQL*Loader discard file
TNSNAMES.ORA

questions.explanation: AWR (and ASH for second-by-second active session history) pinpoints wait-event bottlenecks and top resource-consuming SQL.

questions.prompt: Why can using literals instead of bind variables in high-frequency OLTP SQL degrade Oracle 12c Shared Pool performance?

options.text: Literals disable primary keys
Each distinct literal forces a hard parse, causing library cache latch/mutex contention and Shared Pool fragmentation
Bind variables prevent index usage always
Literals bypass redo logging

questions.explanation: Bind variables allow cursor sharing and soft parses, protecting the Shared Pool from hard-parse CPU storms.

rubric.label: Understands hard parse vs soft parse
Diagnoses Shared Pool / library cache contention

questions.prompt: In Oracle 12c, which dynamic performance view column directly identifies the session ID blocking a waiting session?

options.text: V$SESSION.BLOCKING_SESSION
DBA_TABLES.PCT_FREE
V$DATAFILE.BYTES
USER_SEQUENCES.CACHE_SIZE

questions.explanation: Querying `V$SESSION` for `BLOCKING_SESSION IS NOT NULL` (along with `EVENT`, `SQL_ID`, and `SECONDS_IN_WAIT`) immediately locates the root blocker.

questions.prompt: What does the Oracle wait event `enq: TX - row lock contention` indicate?

options.text: Disk controller firmware failure
A session is waiting to modify a row currently locked by an uncommitted transaction in another session (or unique-key/ITL contention)
The listener port 1521 is closed
Archive log destination is empty

questions.explanation: TX row lock contention occurs when Session B updates/deletes a row held by Session A's open transaction until A commits or rolls back.

questions.prompt: How does Oracle 12c automatically handle a deadlock (`ORA-00060: deadlock detected while waiting for resource`)?

options.text: Hangs the entire database permanently until reboot
Automatically detects the cycle, rolls back the single offending statement in one session, and writes a trace file
Kills all connected users
Drops the locked table

questions.explanation: Oracle breaks deadlocks within seconds by aborting one statement (not the whole transaction) and logging a trace graph for RCA.

rubric.label: Knows trace file is generated for RCA

questions.prompt: Why does an unindexed Foreign Key column on a child table frequently cause table-level `TM` lock contention in Oracle 12c?

options.text: Oracle requires a full table lock on the child table when deleting or updating the parent primary key if the child FK lacks an index
Foreign keys cannot exist without a bitmap index
Unindexed FKs disable ARCHIVELOG mode
Oracle refuses INSERT into child tables

questions.explanation: Indexing child foreign-key columns eliminates full-table TM locks during parent DELETE/PK-UPDATE operations.

rubric.label: Diagnoses unindexed FK TM lock contention

questions.prompt: Select ALL artifacts a DBA should inspect during a production Oracle 12c incident RCA.

options.text: Alert log and ADR incident/deadlock trace files
ASH / AWR wait event and SQL_ID history around the incident window
Recent DDL, statistics gathering, or application deployment changes
Deleting trace files before reading them

questions.explanation: Correlating alert logs, trace files, ASH/AWR telemetry, and change logs produces an evidence-backed RCA.

rubric.label: Collects ADR, AWR/ASH, and change evidence

questions.prompt: Production checkout is stalled with 45 sessions waiting on `enq: TX - row lock contention`. Describe your step-by-step live triage, safe mitigation, and post-incident RCA.
questions.explanation: Query V$SESSION/V$SQL to find the root blocker and its application owner, confirm impact before `ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION 'sid,serial#' IMMEDIATE`, and follow up on long uncommitted transactions or unindexed FKs in RCA.

rubric.label: Coordinates safe session termination and RCA
